point_types.does_not_earn: A numerator difference written in the wrong order, an unsquared denominator, or a derivative formed as the ratio of the two derivatives. sg-25:21 states that a response applying the quotient rule but not the chain rule does not earn the second structure point.
point_types.earns: A derivative of a ratio presented with the denominator's derivative subtracted in the numerator and the denominator squared, whether the ratio is built from named functions or from an explicit expression. samples-14-q3:1 awards two of the three points in the part to this derivative expression before any value is substituted. sg-25:21 states that a response correctly applying the quotient rule, together with the chain rule, to a separated solution earns the corresponding structure points.

point_types.name: Quotient rule applied to a ratio of two functions
point_types.notation_requirements: No special notation requirement stated in the rubrics reviewed.
point_types.notes: Minted for the documented point-type gap in which the quotient rule was mapped onto BC-PT-99022, the product rule point. Tagged single-source because no rubric in the corpus names the quotient rule as a point of its own; samples-14-q3:1 awards the expression without naming the rule and sg-25:21 names it only inside an alternate-approach note.
point_types.precision_rules: Not a reported-value point, so the three-decimal rule does not apply.

point_types.does_not_earn: A denominator factored without the numerators solved for, or an antiderivative written straight from the unfactored rational expression. The decomposition point is separate from the antiderivative point in both rubrics, so one cannot cover the other (sg-19:6, samples-15-q5:1).
point_types.earns: The rational integrand rewritten as a sum of terms over the linear factors of the denominator with both numerators determined. sg-19:6 awards one of the three points in the part to the decomposition alone, before any antiderivative is written. samples-15-q5:1 awards two of the four points in its part to the decomposition.

point_types.dependency_on_other_points: samples-15-q5:1 awards the slope point and the tangent line equation point independently within the same part.
point_types.does_not_earn: A line written through the point with an unstated or incorrect slope, or a slope reported with no equation when the part asks for an equation; the two points are awarded separately (samples-15-q5:1).
point_types.earns: Two separable pieces of work: the value of the derivative at the stated input, and an equation of the line through the point on the curve with that slope. samples-15-q5:1 awards one point for the slope and a second for the tangent line equation, so a correct slope earns its point even when no line is written.

point_types.does_not_earn: Segments drawn at points other than the indicated ones, or a solution curve drawn in place of the field; the rubric scores the segments at the indicated points only (samples-15-q4:1).
point_types.earns: Short segments drawn at the indicated points whose slopes match the differential equation there. samples-15-q4:1 splits the two points of the part by the value of the independent variable, so the segments at each value of that variable are scored as a group.
